entries.name: Stonehenge
entries.description: Prehistoric monument, consisting of rings of stones, with the outermost ring made up of large stone columns. Believed to have been an astronomical observatory.

entries.name: Avebury
entries.description: Great standing stones encircle a grassy hollow. Raised in Britain long before written records, this vast monument holds smaller circles within it. What ceremonies once drew people here?

entries.name: Rosetta Stone
entries.description: Black basalt slab bearing the same inscription in three languages- ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics, a simpler ancient Egyptian writing system, and Greek.

entries.name: Khufu Pyramid
entries.description: Tomb of the Pharaoh Khufu, a pyramid measuring 481 feet high with a square base 756 feet wide. The four sides face the north, south, east and west.

entries.name: Crocodile
entries.description: Fierce amphibious predator armored with hard leather skin, the crocodile sometimes reaches a length of 20 feet. With its powerful jaws, it can rip into livestock animals and even humans with one bite.

entries.name: Nubia Pyramid
entries.description: Pyramid built by the ancient Cush in northern Africa. Though it's relatively small, with a 30 by 30 foot square base, it has distinctively steep sides.

entries.name: Tessisat Falls
entries.description: This remote waterfall is 140 feet high and is found near the source of the Blue Nile.

entries.name: Baobab
entries.description: Huge tree with many useful qualities. The bark can be used to fashion rope or cloth, the fruit is edible, and the trunk itself is so large it can be used for storage or even shelter.

entries.name: Pteranodon
entries.description: A dark-colored bird whose bat-like wings measure 6 feet across. It's noted for its large beak and sharp teeth.

entries.name: Victoria Falls
entries.description: The Zambezi River plunges 400 feet into Lake Victoria, forming Victoria Falls. Lake Victoria is believed to be the source of the Nile River.

entries.name: Diogo's Monument
entries.description: A tall stone monument with inscriptions in Latin, Portuguese, and Arabic. Erected when Diogo Cam discovered the Congo.

entries.name: Ant Hill
entries.description: These small ant castles, in their various shapes, often surpass the architectural feats of man.

entries.name: Clay Mosque
entries.description: Supposedly, the ruins of a golden city in the Sahara. Time has taken its toll, but the work of conscientious desert dwellers have helped preserve the ancient structure.

entries.name: Armadillo
entries.description: Animal with bony plates on its back. When threatened, it curls up to cover its soft unprotected abdomen.

entries.name: Moquele Mubembe
entries.description: The locals of Lake Tele have claimed to have seen this dinosaur from time to time. It's believed to be herbivorous and about 15 feet long.

entries.name: Moonbow
entries.description: A rainbow that shines gold and white in the dark night. Legend says that this beautiful, mysterious vision brings good luck to those who see it.

entries.name: Quagga
entries.description: A horse-like creature related to the zebra, but with no stripes on its hind portion. It takes its name from the sound it makes, {Kwahaha.}

entries.name: Diaz's Monument
entries.description: Stone monument at the Cape of Good Hope on the southern tip of Africa. It was erected by Bartholomew Diaz and remains a symbol of brave sea adventurers.

entries.name: Big Zimbabwe
entries.description: The name means [large rock house]. It proves that there was once a glorious dynasty in this area.

entries.name: Mandrill
entries.description: Monkey with a colorful face resembling that of a human. It has a beard, purple bottom, and a short tail.

entries.name: Dodo
entries.description: A bird the size of a turkey, with a large hooked bill. Its wings are very small, making it incapable of flight.

entries.name: Chameleon
entries.description: Lizard with the amazing ability to change its color to match its surroundings. It's quite adept at capturing insects with its long and sticky tongue.

entries.name: Papyrus
entries.description: Tall water plant that was used to make a form of paper in ancient Egypt.

entries.name: Burning Water
entries.description: Strange black liquid that springs out from underground in desert areas. It has a bad smell and burns easily.

entries.name: Mohenjo-Daro
entries.description: Ruins of a city dating from the time of the Indus civilization. Built around a dome-shaped Buddhist shrine on a hilltop, this city probably was a commercial center during the Bronze Age.

entries.name: King Cobra
entries.description: The world's largest poisonous snake. When disturbed, it extends its ribs behind its head to form a flaring hood.

entries.name: Inle Lake
entries.description: The people who live here have built their homes and fields on the island that floats on the surface of this lake.

entries.name: Ayutthaya's Buddha
entries.description: One of many busts of Buddha found in Siam, which has several temples and statues dedicated to him.

entries.name: Hornbill
entries.description: Friendly large-billed bird that makes a hissing sound to intimidate its enemies. It sometimes grows up to 60 inches in height.

entries.name: Angkor Wat
entries.description: Ruins of a temple constructed by Khmer during the 12th century. The name means [temple of the capital.] Measuring 2800 by 3300 feet, it contains concentric walled courtyards surrounding a central structure of beautiful towers.

entries.name: Kalavinka
entries.description: A bird of legend said to have the face of a beautiful girl. Its sweet singing can make people forget everything, even their own names.

entries.name: Plant Worm
entries.description: A strange insect which transforms itself into a fungus during the summer. It is highly valued in China as a tonic and an elixir.

entries.name: Toro Ruins
entries.description: Ruins of farming villages dating from around 300 B.C. The villages had rice fields orderly divided by strong ridges and storehouses with elevated floors.

entries.name: Namahage
entries.description: Fabled demons that kidnap and devour bad children. The legend is told in a traditional festival where men disguise themselves as demons to scare the town's children.

entries.name: Qian Ling
entries.description: Empress Zetian Wuhou's tomb. A hill with a circumference of 25 miles was turned into this huge tomb where all her treasures are buried.

entries.name: Great Wall
entries.description: 1500 miles long and averaging 25 feet high, this truly is a great wall. It was constructed over many generations by Chinese rulers as a defense against raids by nomads in the north.

entries.name: Hedgehog
entries.description: A small mammal with an arsenal of long prickly spines on its back. It rolls itself into a ball when threatened.

entries.name: Panda
entries.description: A large bear-like black and white animal found at high altitudes in mountainous regions. It's friendly and feeds on bamboo.

entries.name: Passenger Pigeon
entries.description: A beautiful pigeon with slate blue wings and a russet breast. They migrate in large flocks every spring. People say that this species will never become extinct. (Or will it?)

entries.name: Totem Pole
entries.description: Large wooden pole carved with the designs of animals. It symbolizes the status of the chief, and is sometimes used as a sign of the tribe.

entries.name: Jade Mask
entries.description: A mask encrusted with small pieces of jade. Its eye holes give it a somewhat ominous appearance.

entries.name: Guatavita Lake
entries.description: A holy place for the Muisca, who throw gold and emeralds into the lake when their new king ascends the throne.

entries.name: Cactus
entries.description: Spiny, fleshy plant that grows up to 6 feet tall. This unique plant is well-adapted for arid climates.

entries.name: Iguana
entries.description: A large scaly lizard, measuring about 6 feet in length. The row of leathery spines on its back make it look like a fierce dinosaur, but it's actually a gentle creature.

entries.name: Venus' Flytrap
entries.description: Insect-eating plant with a jaw-shaped flower that bears sharp spines and secretes a sweet liquid. Once its jaws snap shut they won't reopen until the prey has been digested.

entries.name: Niagara Falls
entries.description: A magnificent waterfall, about 158 feet high and 3010 feet wide. Ancient people must have thought that the edge of the earth looks something like this.

entries.name: Amazon Water Lily
entries.description: An aquatic plant with giant floating leaves and large flowers. The leaves measure over 6 feet in diameter and are so strong that they can bear the weight of a small child.

entries.name: Anaconda
entries.description: A gigantic serpent. Adults may grow 19 feet long and weigh as much as 235 pounds. They are found near the water and crush their victims by constricting them in their coils.

entries.name: Pororoca
entries.description: An enormous tidal wave that occurs during the new moon in April. Locals say that huge waves may reach over 16 feet high and wash everything away from the shore.

entries.name: Matamata
entries.description: A spiny turtle with a large diamond-shaped head and an irregular, rugged shell.

entries.name: Balsa
entries.description: A primitive vessel used for local inter-tribal trading. This raft has a grass hut mounted on top and uses a square sail.

entries.name: Piranha
entries.description: The terror of South American rivers. It is not uncommon for these groups of fish to devour people or domesticated animals that try to cross their river.

entries.name: Tarantula
entries.description: A large hairy poisonous spider that feeds on birds and small animals.

entries.name: Archaeopteryx
entries.description: A reptilian bird thought to be an ancestor of today's birds. It had four legs and was unable to fly, but it is believed that this bird-reptile could glide.

entries.name: Gold Frog
entries.description: A tiny frog with beautiful golden skin that secretes a mysterious poison. Locals believe that this rare frog will guide one to a legendary land of gold.

entries.name: Toucan
entries.description: A loud-squawking bird with a huge, brightly colored beak. It feeds chiefly on fruit.

entries.name: Clay Monster
entries.description: A clay figure of a monster with a large head and fangs.

entries.name: Giant Ground Sloth
entries.description: A slow-moving, hairy mammal with sharp claws. Rumor has it this 20 feet tall creature walks upright and feeds on leaves and branches.

entries.name: Anteater
entries.description: A toothless mammal with powerful claws on its front feet and a long tongue that comes in handy for catching ants - the mainstay of its diet. Its long tail accounts for half of its 6 foot length.

entries.name: Leon Penguin
entries.description: A flightless goose-sized bird that uses its wings to swim. Found in large flocks, it was discovered by the Portuguese navigator, Leon Franco, about 20 years ago. Well, that's what some people say.

entries.name: Vampire Bat
entries.description: A large bat with a 12 inch wingspan. It uses its sharp teeth to make a shallow wound on its prey, secretes a liquid to prevent the wound from closing, and feeds on its blood.

entries.name: Lake Titicaca
entries.description: The world's highest lake at an altitude of 12,500 feet in the Andes Mountains. The Aztecs believe that a god lives in this lake.

entries.name: Temple of the Sun
entries.description: A pyramid-shaped shrine in the central Andes, with distinctive frontal stairs climbing 33 feet to the top.

entries.name: Terracotta Figure
entries.description: This large sculpture represents a legendary hero worshipped by local tribes. Its sculpting technique and intricate design prove that this area has a highly advanced culture.

entries.name: Stone Ball
entries.description: A perfectly spherical stone measuring about 6.5 feet in diameter. Its use is unknown.

entries.name: Mural of Marnalico
entries.description: A mural of warriors and hunting gods.

entries.name: Popol Vuh
entries.description: A manuscript of Mayan legends, describing their philosophy, cosmology, and history.

entries.name: Crystal Skull
entries.description: An elaborately sculptured crystal skull used for generations in rituals by tribal leaders.

entries.name: Stone Face
entries.description: A stone bust excavated from Tenochtitlan.

entries.name: Monument of the Sun
entries.description: A round stone monument symbolizing the sun and the seasons. It represents the Aztec people's concept of the universe.

entries.name: Mexican Beaded Lizard
entries.description: A large lizard with black and yellow bead-like scales. Its secret weapon is its ability to produce poison in its mouth.

entries.name: Bison
entries.description: A large wild bull that can weigh almost a ton. It is hunted for both food and its hide, which can be used to make leather. Such great numbers roam the plains that it's hard to imagine them ever becoming extinct.

entries.name: Prairie dog
entries.description: Ground-dwelling squirrel-like mammals 11 - 16 inches long. They make their home underground in a complex system of interconnecting burrows with many entrances.

entries.name: Borobudur
entries.description: The ruins of a major Buddhist monument. It consists of eight diminishing tiers of terraces connected by stairways. The walls of the corridors are lined with intricately carved relief sculptures.

entries.name: Python
entries.description: A giant snake that can grow over 33 feet long in the jungle. After constricting and suffocating an animal, the python swallows its prey whole.

entries.name: Komodo Dragon
entries.description: A giant slow-moving lizard found only in secluded parts of Indonesia that can grow up to 10 feet long. It uses its long, sharp claws and jagged teeth to attack animals even as large as a small deer.

entries.name: Kangaroo
entries.description: Its long fat tail and powerful hind legs help this animal hip-hop along. The newly born infants, still small and pinkish, crawl into a pouch on the mother's belly and remain there during infancy.

entries.name: Frilled Lizard
entries.description: A lizard with a large umbrella-like frill. It rises up and opens the frill to intimidate enemies and runs away only on its rear legs.

entries.name: Ayers Rock
entries.description: A legend says that there is a humongous red monolith in the center of this continent.

entries.name: Tazmanian Devil
entries.description: A 30 inch long nocturnal animal that feeds on small animals and carrion. It hides in the cracks of rocks and trees.

entries.name: Koala
entries.description: A tree-dwelling marsupial mammal that only eats the leaves of the eucalyptus tree. Koala young spend their first 6 months in their mother's pouch, feeding on predigested eucalyptus leaves.

entries.name: Kiwi
entries.description: Named for its cry, this is a flightless, nocturnal bird with a small head and a long, slender bill that has nostrils near the tip. It uses its highly developed sense of smell to find its food.

entries.name: Greater Bird of Paradise
entries.description: The male of this beautiful bird has a yellow head, long tail and dark-green throat, but the female has only short feathers and is rather dull in color.

entries.name: Stone Buddha
entries.description: A huge statue of Buddha carved out of the side of a mountain.

entries.name: Pitcher Plant
entries.description: A plant that feeds on insects by trapping and digesting them in its pitcher-like leaves.

entries.name: Tree Snake
entries.description: A slender snake about 3 feet long. The name comes from the fact that it makes its home in trees.

entries.name: Durian
entries.description: A fruit that is covered with sharp needles. Some say that it is the most delicious of all tropical forest fruits, but it smells so bad that most don't dare taste it.

entries.name: Moa
entries.description: An ostrich-like bird incapable of flight, measuring over 10 feet in height. Its massive and well-developed hind legs help it run very fast.

entries.name: Great Auk
entries.description: A flightless bird about 30 inches long that makes its home near Greenland. Fishermen hunt this bird for its tasty meat.

entries.name: Aurora
entries.description: A luminous atmospheric phenomenon seen in the night sky. Its awesome curtain-like display is constantly changing. While it's something special to see, the magnetic storms that occur with it can disturb your compass.

entries.name: Stellar's Sea Cow
entries.description: A large water mammal about 10 feet long. The head resembles a seal and its rear part has a fish-like shape. Locals say its meat is delicious.

entries.name: Blue Whale
entries.description: The largest animal in the world, sometimes reaching a length of 30 meters and weighing over 150 tons.

entries.name: Mammoth
entries.description: A legendary giant elephant with a coat of brown wool and long tusks that curve upward.

entries.name: Saber-toothed Tiger
entries.description: A large carnivorous animal about 6 feet long. Its enormous, blade-like upper teeth extend 7 inches below its lower jaw.

entries.name: Fruit Bat
entries.description: Just as the name suggests, this bat lives off of fruit. It is a very rare delicacy at tables throughout the area.

entries.name: Indo-Pacific Cowrie
entries.description: A rare snail with a beautiful shell that lives deep in the sea. Its shell is used as an amulet by tribal leaders and shamans in the area.

entries.name: Nasiped
entries.description: A creature rumored to resemble a mouse that walks upside down using its highly developed nose. This odd creature is probably fantastical.

entries.name: Giant Tortoise
entries.description: A large, slow-moving tortoise that can weigh as much as 500 pounds. Its domed shell sometimes grows as long as three feet and serves as protection for its elephant-like skin.

entries.name: Moai
entries.description: Giant stone statues ranging from 15 to 60 feet high. They're carved with large faces, long ears and short bodies.

entries.name: Pompey's Pillar
entries.description: In Alexandria, a towering red granite column rises above the broken remains of an ancient temple. Raised in honor of a Roman emperor, it is now known to sailors by Pompey's name.

entries.name: Goliath Tigerfish
entries.description: Deep in the Congo's powerful rivers swims a silver hunter armed with long, daggerlike teeth. It strikes smaller fish amid the current, and even skilled boatmen keep their hands clear of its jaws.

entries.name: Clay Dogu
entries.description: A tiny clay figure with wide eyes and strange patterned limbs rests in the northern hills of Japan. Its ancient maker left no explanation; some believe such images served a role in healing rites.

entries.name: Divi-Divi Tree
entries.description: On the dry Caribbean shore grows a crooked tree, bent as though forever bowing to the wind. Its twisted seedpods contain a rich tanning substance prized by those who work with hides.

entries.name: Maya Cacao Cup
entries.description: A painted clay vessel bears noble figures and fine ornaments from the old Maya cities. Cups like this held cacao, beaten into a dark froth and shared at feasts and important gatherings.

entries.name: Kata Tjuta
entries.description: Beyond the red desert plain rise immense rounded domes of stone, divided by narrow gorges. These hills hold deep meaning for the Anangu people, whose sacred stories are their own to share.

entries.name: Southern Cassowary
entries.description: In the forests of New Guinea stalks a tall, flightless bird with a hornlike crown and a bright blue neck. Its powerful feet bear sharp claws, while fallen fruit makes up much of its food.

entries.name: Walrus
entries.description: On the icebound northern seas rests a massive, whiskered beast with two ivory tusks. Its sensitive bristles help it seek shellfish beneath the cold, shallow water of the Bering Sea.

entries.name: Marine Iguana
entries.description: Upon the black volcanic shores lives a dark lizard that plunges into the surf. Unlike its landbound kin, it grazes on seaweed, then returns to sun-warmed rocks to recover its heat.

entries.name: Step Pyramid of Djoser
entries.description: In the desert south of Cairo rises a great stone tomb of six rising tiers. Built for King Djoser, the pyramid stands among courtyards and shrines, a marvel of Egypt's oldest royal builders.

entries.name: Dugong
entries.description: Off the eastern African shore a gentle sea grazer rises to breathe, then sinks among the seagrass beds. Its broad muzzle and heavy, fluked body have inspired many a sailor's tale.

entries.name: Xanadu Ruins
entries.description: On the windswept grasslands north of China lie the walls of Xanadu, once a seat of Kublai Khan. Earth banks still trace the palaces and streets where Mongol and Chinese traditions met.

entries.name: Prairie Blazing Star
entries.description: Across the open central plains rises a slender wand of rose-purple blossoms above the grass. Its deep roots hold fast through dry seasons, and winged insects crowd its bright flowers.

entries.name: Greater Rhea
entries.description: Across the grassy plains of southern South America runs a tall, flightless bird. Long legs carry it swiftly through the pampas, while its broad wings spread as it turns to escape danger.

entries.name: Banten Girang Ruins
entries.description: Near Java's western strait lie old banks and stone-cut chambers beside a river. These are traces of Banten Girang, a vanished settlement that once watched the busy waterways of the island.

entries.name: Western Quoll
entries.description: In the woodlands of southwestern Australia prowls a spotted night hunter with a pointed face. It shelters in hollow logs by day, then seeks insects and small prey beneath the stars.

entries.name: Palm Cockatoo
entries.description: In the northern forests of Australia a great black cockatoo raises its long crest above a red cheek. Its mighty beak cracks hard nuts, and its deep voice carries through the treetops.

entries.name: Sun Dogs
entries.description: In the northern sky two bright phantoms sometimes flank the low sun, as if three suns shone at once. These strange lights appear where sunlight bends through tiny ice crystals in the air.

entries.name: Chamorro Slingstone
entries.description: A smooth stone, shaped like a small spindle and sharpened at both ends, is found among relics of the Mariana Islands. Skilled islanders cast such stones from woven slings with remarkable force.

entries.name: Meroe Pyramids
entries.description: Sharp pyramids rise from the Nubian sands beside the old kingdom of Kush. Though smaller than Egypt's, these royal tombs stand in long rows beneath the desert sun.

entries.name: Aye-Aye
entries.description: On Madagascar lives a strange night creature with huge ears, bright eyes, and a thin tapping finger. It creeps through the forest after dark in search of grubs hidden in wood.

entries.name: Baba Gurgur Flame
entries.description: From stony ground beyond the gulf, a flame bursts where gases seep from the earth. Travelers have long marveled at this fire, which can burn without any wood to feed it.

entries.name: Dholavira
entries.description: Stone reservoirs, gates, and ordered streets fill this ancient city of the western Indus world. Its builders mastered water and trade in a dry land ringed by salt flats.

entries.name: Sumatran Orangutan
entries.description: High in the rain forest swings a great red ape with long arms and thoughtful eyes. It moves from branch to branch slowly, feeding on fruit in the humid canopy.

entries.name: Ginkgo Tree
entries.description: This ancient tree bears fan-shaped leaves unlike those of any other broadleaf. In autumn its crown turns gold, and its kind is said to descend from a far older world.

entries.name: Great Lakes
entries.description: A chain of vast inland seas spreads across the northern forests. Cold blue waters meet rocky shores and pine-clad islands, forming one of the grandest freshwater realms on earth.

entries.name: Muisca Tunjo
entries.description: A small gold figure stands with rigid limbs and a solemn face. Such offerings were shaped by the Muisca and placed at sacred sites as gifts to powers beyond the ordinary world.

entries.name: Rafflesia
entries.description: On the jungle floor blooms a giant red flower speckled in pale dots. Its heavy petals open around a deep center, making it one of the most astonishing blossoms in the tropics.

entries.name: Atlantic Puffin
entries.description: Upon windy sea cliffs stands a black-and-white bird with a bright beak and orange feet. It nests in burrows near the North Atlantic, returning to land in the summer season.

entries.name: Danakil Depression
entries.description: A harsh land of salt, steam, and burning color spreads across the desert floor. Strange pools and smoking vents make this one of the most otherworldly sights in Africa.

entries.name: Indian Peafowl
entries.description: This splendid bird walks the dry plains in gleaming blue and green. When it opens its great tail, a hundred jeweled eyes seem to shimmer in the sun.

entries.name: Sukhothai Ruins
entries.description: Broken walls, lotus ponds, and serene Buddha images remain from an early Siamese capital. Quiet temples and towers still rise above the plain.

entries.name: Saola
entries.description: In the shadowed forests of the Annamite mountains lives a rare horned beast scarcely seen by men. Its long straight horns and pale face mark it as a wonder of the wild.

entries.name: Olmec Jade Celt
entries.description: A polished green celt of sacred stone was shaped by ancient hands and treasured in ceremony. Its smooth surface and rich color made jade a symbol of power and life.

entries.name: Electric Eel
entries.description: In muddy tropical waters glides a long fish able to unleash a numbing shock. Fishermen fear its hidden strength where roots and reeds darken the river.

entries.name: Magellanic Penguin
entries.description: Along cold southern shores stands a black-and-white bird with a pink band at the eye. It comes ashore in great colonies and dives swiftly after fish in the surf.

entries.name: Sacsayhuaman
entries.description: High above Cuzco stand mighty terraces built from enormous interlocking stones. Their precise joints and commanding height show the skill of the Inca builders.

entries.name: Nutmeg Tree
entries.description: This spice tree bears pale fruits that split to reveal a dark seed wrapped in crimson lace. From these fragrant kernels come prized seasonings sought across the seas.

entries.name: Narwhal
entries.description: Beneath the drifting ice swims a pale whale with a long spear-like tusk. Mariners of the far north prize tales of this strange beast of the frozen sea.

entries.name: Mergui Archipelago
entries.description: West of the Malay Peninsula lies a maze of green islands amid clear blue waters. Forests hide deep coves and quiet beaches, while coral gardens flourish beneath the waves.

entries.name: Sannai-Maruyama Ruins
entries.description: In northern Japan lie the traces of a vast ancient village. Great timber posts, earth pits, and old hearths mark a settlement whose people lived here long before the age of samurai.

entries.name: Etowah Mounds
entries.description: Beside a river rise tall earthen mounds built by the people of the southeastern lands. Broad plazas and high platforms reveal a great center of ceremony, farming, and trade.

entries.name: Kapok Tree
entries.description: A mighty trunk towers above the tropical forest, held upright by enormous roots like wooden walls. High in its crown hang pods filled with a soft, pale fiber.

entries.name: Blue-footed Booby
entries.description: A bold seabird rests upon rocks above the Pacific surf. Its feet shine an astonishing blue, and it dives like an arrow into the sea to catch its prey.

entries.name: Atacama Desert
entries.description: Between the Pacific and the high Andes stretches a barren realm of stone, salt, and red hills. Whole valleys may wait years for rain beneath a cloudless sky.

entries.name: Zenu Gold Pectoral
entries.description: A broad golden pendant gleams with hammered patterns and the forms of river creatures. Metalworkers of the northern lands shaped such treasures for display and ceremony.

entries.name: Bare-nosed Wombat
entries.description: On the cool wooded island south of Australia lives a stout burrowing grazer. With powerful claws it digs deep shelters and feeds on grass in the evening.

entries.name: Tuatara
entries.description: On lonely islets near New Zealand dwells a spiny-backed reptile with the look of ancient days. It hides in burrows and moves quietly among seabird colonies.

entries.name: Oceanic Manta Ray
entries.description: Across the warm ocean glides a giant ray with wings like dark sails. It sweeps through the blue water with slow strokes, drawing tiny food from the sea.

entries.name: Sankore Mosque
entries.description: Beyond the sandy streets of Timbuktu stands a mosque built of earth and timber. Travelers gather here to pray and study, while scholars discuss books carried across the desert.

entries.name: Humpback Whale
entries.description: In the warm waters east of Madagascar, an immense whale rises in a spray of foam. Long white-edged flippers cut the sea as it rolls, then its dark body vanishes below the waves.

entries.name: Banteay Srei
entries.description: Deep among the Khmer temples stands a shrine of red sandstone, its doorways covered in fine carvings. Every lintel bears figures and curling vines cut with astonishing skill.

entries.name: Longmen Grottoes
entries.description: Along the cliffs by a river, countless sacred figures have been carved into stone. Serene Buddhas sit within deep niches, their faces watching the waters flow far below.

entries.name: American Black Bear
entries.description: In the broad forests of eastern North America wanders a powerful black-furred bear. It turns stones for insects and feeds on berries and nuts before the cold of winter.

entries.name: Amazon Flood Forest
entries.description: When the great Amazon rises, river water sweeps between trees until the forest becomes a maze of channels. Canoes pass among trunks while fish swim where roots once stood dry.

entries.name: Guarani Pottery
entries.description: A finely shaped earthen vessel bears dark bands and painted lines. Such pottery is made by Guarani communities of the southern river lands, to hold food and water in daily life.

entries.name: Saltwater Crocodile
entries.description: In the creeks and mangroves of the eastern islands lurks a mighty reptile, armored with rough scales. Only its eyes show above the tide before it strikes without warning.

entries.name: Philippine Eagle
entries.description: A towering eagle watches the forest from a high branch, its wild crest raised above a hooked beak. With broad wings it glides between the mountains of these green islands.

entries.name: Orongo Village
entries.description: Above the breakers on a lonely Pacific island lie low stone houses set into a grassy crater rim. Carved rocks recall the ceremonies of a people far from other shores.

entries.name: Frankincense Tree
entries.description: From the stony slopes of the Horn rises a crooked tree whose bark yields fragrant tears of resin. Caravans prize this incense, carrying its scent to distant shrines and markets.

entries.name: Giant Pangolin
entries.description: In the forested country by the great Congo rivers walks a giant creature clad in overlapping scales. Its long claws tear into termite mounds, while a sticky tongue gathers the insects within.

entries.name: Golden Snub-Nosed Monkey
entries.description: Among the high forests of central China climbs a monkey with golden fur and a striking blue face. Its thick coat guards against cold mountain air, and its troop calls from the treetops.

entries.name: Hoatzin
entries.description: Above the flooded forests of northern South America perches a curious bird with a ragged crest. It feeds on leaves and gives off a strong odor, earning a strange reputation among boatmen.

entries.name: Black Caiman
entries.description: Hidden in the dark channels of the Amazon lies a mighty black caiman. Only its eyes and armored brow break the water as it watches prey from the shadows.

entries.name: Huemul Deer
entries.description: In the cold mountains of southern Chile roams a sturdy deer with short legs and branching antlers. It keeps to wooded slopes and rocky valleys where few travelers pass.

entries.name: El Cano Stone Circles
entries.description: Across the river plains of Panama stand weathered stone columns and ancient burial grounds. The people who raised them left carved stones and offerings beneath the tropical earth.

entries.name: Maya Eccentric Flint
entries.description: A blade of flint has been chipped into a winding shape, with slender points that serve no common tool. Maya craftsmen placed such extraordinary works in sacred offerings.

entries.name: Leang-Leang Caves
entries.description: Within limestone caves on the island of Sulawesi, red handprints and figures mark ancient stone walls. The painted signs endure in the cool darkness far beyond the memory of their makers.

entries.name: Polar Bear
entries.description: Upon the frozen shores of Greenland prowls a huge white bear, its broad paws spreading over snow and ice. It hunts seals at the edge of the sea, disappearing against the pale horizon.

entries.name: Benin Earthworks
entries.description: Great banks of red earth and deep moats surround the ancient kingdom of Benin. These mighty walls run past forest and village, guarding the roads to the royal city.

entries.name: Bandiagara Cliffs
entries.description: Towering sandstone cliffs break the dry plains of Mali. Villages cling to their ledges, with small houses and granaries sheltered beneath walls of glowing red rock.

entries.name: Hartmann's Zebra
entries.description: Upon the dry mountain slopes of southwestern Africa roams a striped wild horse. Its narrow hoofprints cross rocky gullies as it searches for grass and precious water.

entries.name: Doum Palm
entries.description: Beside the Nile and dry wadis grows a palm with forked trunks and fanlike leaves. Its hard fruits and strong fibers are prized by the peoples of the river lands.

entries.name: Pallas's Cat
entries.description: A small, thick-furred wildcat hides among stones on the cold northern steppes of China. Its flat face and rounded ears make it look fierce, though it seldom shows itself.

entries.name: Scarlet Ibis
entries.description: Bright red birds gather in the mangrove shallows of the southern Caribbean. Their long curved bills probe the mud while flocks glow like embers against the green coast.

entries.name: Arapaima
entries.description: Beneath the brown waters of the Amazon moves an immense fish plated in heavy scales. It rises to gulp air before sinking again into the flooded forest channels.

entries.name: Monte Alban
entries.description: High above a valley in southern Mexico lie great stone terraces and courts. The Zapotec built this hilltop city with temples, tombs and wide plazas beneath the open sky.

entries.name: Javan Tiger
entries.description: In the thick forests of Java moves a fierce striped cat, silent and heavy-footed. Hunters fear its sudden leap from the undergrowth, where its orange coat vanishes in shadow.

entries.name: Whale Shark
entries.description: Far east of the Philippine islands swims a gentle giant marked with pale spots. Though greater than many ships, this broad-mouthed shark feeds on tiny drifting sea life.

entries.name: Nile Perch
entries.description: In the upper Nile swims a giant fish with silver scales and a ravenous mouth. It waits in deep river channels, then strikes at smaller fish with startling speed.

entries.name: African Rock Python
entries.description: Near the lakes and rivers of eastern Africa coils a mighty patterned serpent. Hidden among reeds and rocks, it waits for prey before closing its powerful body around it.

entries.name: Lake Tanganyika
entries.description: Between the steep ridges of the African Rift stretches a vast blue lake. Its waters run for hundreds of miles between rocky shores and shelter a world of strange fish.

entries.name: Kasai River
entries.description: Across the heart of central Africa flows a great brown river, gathering many streams beneath the rainforest. Broad channels wind among green banks on their way to the Congo.

entries.name: Blombos Cave
entries.description: On the southern African coast a sheltered cavern holds traces of people from ages long past. Shells, stone tools, and red ochre reveal the work of skilled ancient hands.

entries.name: Spectacled Bear
entries.description: In the misty forests of the Andes lives a black bear with pale rings around its eyes. It climbs steep slopes and trees to feed on fruit and tender plants.

entries.name: Maned Wolf
entries.description: Across the grasslands of southern South America walks a tall reddish hunter on long black legs. It hunts small creatures and fruit in the open country at dusk.

entries.name: Desert Bighorn
entries.description: In the jagged mountains of the western deserts climbs a powerful sheep with curled horns. It leaps among dry ledges where few other creatures can keep their footing.

entries.name: California Sea Otter
entries.description: Along the cold Pacific shore floats a small furred swimmer, cracking shellfish upon a stone. It rests among kelp beds beyond the surf and dives with nimble paws.

entries.name: Greater Bilby
entries.description: A shy night-dweller of Australia's dry country has long ears, a pointed snout, and strong digging claws. It leaves winding tracks beside burrows in the red sand.

entries.name: Cederberg Rock Art
entries.description: In sheltered caves north of the Cape, red and ochre figures of eland and hunters cover the stone. These ancient paintings preserve traces of the San people's sacred traditions.

entries.name: Bacalar Lagoon
entries.description: Near the southern Yucatan coast lies a long freshwater lagoon, where shallow shelves shine turquoise and deeper waters turn blue. Green forest and marshes fringe its quiet shores.

entries.name: Glyptodon
entries.description: In the plains of the southern continent old bones tell of an enormous armored beast. Its round shell was plated like a fortress, and its heavy tail bore a fearsome weight.

entries.name: Usulutan Vessel
entries.description: An old clay vessel carries winding reddish lines upon a pale body. Potters of the southern Maya region mastered this subtle pattern by keeping parts of the clay free from pigment.

entries.name: Las Labradas
entries.description: On a rocky shore in the west of Mexico, strange spirals, beasts, and human shapes have been carved into dark stone. Ocean waves wash across these signs left by ancient hands.

entries.name: California Condor
entries.description: High above the western mountains circles an immense black bird with bright patches beneath its wings. It sails for hours upon rising air, searching the distant ground below.

entries.name: Platypus
entries.description: In the clear streams of southeastern Australia swims a curious furred creature with a broad bill and webbed feet. It dives among stones, hunting small animals hidden beneath the water.

entries.name: Qalupalik
entries.description: In tales told across the northern ice, a strange being waits in dark water below the frozen shore. People warn travelers to heed the cracking floes and keep clear of treacherous ice.

This classic vessel was first built about two centuries ago. Unfortunately, it doesn't stack up to today's ships.
This durable craft's shallow hull makes it easy to maneuver, but its cargo capacity is limited.
It's large and durable, but I wouldn't use it on the open seas.
It used to be popular in Venice, as even the smallest crew can navigate it with ease.
This is a well-balanced lateen ship. It's perfect for a novice sailor.
This one is easy to handle and makes for smooth sailing over the ocean.
This may be a bit expensive, but it's worth the cost when trading around coastal seas.
This is a mid-size ship with a large cargo space. It's easy to maneuver and suitable for adventurous voyages.
This large trading ship is for the experienced navigator.
This is a battleship, but it's also useful for trading if its payload is kept low. Not for the unseasoned sailor.
For such a large ship, this is quite easy to maneuver. I highly recommend it.
It's quite durable for its size. Ye can even use it when fighting pirates if ye maneuver it carefully.
A small, high-performance sailing ship. It has the capacity to carry guns for battles.
We are proud of this great ship. It combines the storage capacity of a galleon with the mobility of a caravel. A true work of art!
Only a few shipyards have the ability to build this ship. Ye'll never regret buying it.
This is the ultimate ship, but it's only for highly skilled navigators.
Well, this is the only type of ship built in China.

This ship isn't bad. Just remember the payload is high...
No other ship can overcome this floating bastion in close combat.
Galleys are normally battleships, but this one is fast enough to be used for trading, as well.
This huge rowing ship is armored with steel, and has space for lots of guns.
This ship was made for many Japanese warlords. Ye may want to own one, too.
This is only a mid-sized ship. I don't think ye can make it home in this one.
A royal Portuguese fighting caravel. Combining square-rigged speed with heavy broadside culverins, she excels at armed exploration and ocean patrol.
An elite Mediterranean dispatch vessel and corsair hunter. Her sleek hull and lofty lateen sails allow her to outmaneuver any galley in shifting winds.
Constructed from durable Malabar teak for the Carreira da India, this heavily armed Portuguese nau withstands monsoons and pirate fleets alike.
The legendary Nao de China. Built to carry New World silver and Asian silk across the vast Pacific, her cavernous hold is unmatched by any merchant vessel.
A fierce North African corsair cruiser. Built for lightning raids and boarding actions, she packs hundreds of janissaries beneath her sweeping lateen sails.
Modeled after the towering Madre de Deus, this seven-decked super-carrack is a floating castle capable of hauling a king's ransom in spices.
A race-built Elizabethan warship with lowered forecastles and a lengthened keel. Fast, weatherly, and bristling with heavy culverins for gunnery duels.
The pinnacle of royal naval architecture. Carrying three tiers of heavy bronze cannon and gilded stern galleries, she rules the seven seas unchallenged.
A small scouting vessel. Cheap to operate and quick under sail, but its light hull and modest hold will not stand up to a warship.
A caravel strengthened for escort duty. More guns and a tougher hull than a common caravel, at the cost of handling and a larger crew.
A light Mediterranean galley. Turns sharply and carries a useful boarding party, but its small battery and fragile hull demand careful handling.
A Mediterranean merchantman with mixed rigging. A useful hold and modest crew make it a flexible trader, though it cannot match a dedicated warship.
A large trading dhow for long sea routes. Carries a generous cargo with a modest crew, but its broad hull turns slowly and supports few guns.
A compact trader combining a Western-style hull with junk rigging. Handy and economical to sail, but its light hull leaves little margin in a gun battle.
A reinforced junk prepared for naval fighting. Its strong hull and large crew suit boarding actions, but added weight reduces speed and handling.
A great carrack fitted for war. A strong hull, heavy battery and ample crew make a formidable flagship, but it is costly, slow and difficult to turn.
A low-built galleon designed for pursuit. Faster and handier than a common galleon, but its smaller hold, lighter hull and reduced crew limit demand compromises.
A light lateen-rigged caravel inspired by the Nina of 1492. A small crew and sharp handling suit coastal exploration, but the hull and battery are light.
A square-rigged caravel inspired by the Pinta of 1492. Quick under sail with a useful small hold, but less agile than a lateen caravel and lightly protected.
An ocean-going nau inspired by Vasco da Gama's Sao Gabriel. A reinforced hull balances cargo and armament, but needs more sailors than a small explorer.
A great Portuguese India carrack inspired by Santa Catarina do Monte Sinai. Strong protection and a spacious hold combine with heavy guns, but the ship is slow and costly.
